accepted.s: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in which year?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1199.
accepted.tq: Use the date as the direct discriminator among closely related reign events.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: The first inscription of Ganapatideva was issued at Manthena on:
accepted.x: Ganapatideva's first inscription was the Manthena inscription dated 26 December 1199.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact date and place of an inscription.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ganapatideva and the Velanati Chodas:
1. Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka of Nellore jointly killed Prithviswara in 1210.
2. Both rulers assumed the title Prithviswara Shirakhandika Kreeda Vinoda.
3. The Velanati kingdom came to an end in 1210.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Prithviswara was killed in 1210, the joint title was adopted by Ganapatideva and Choda Tikka, and the Velanati kingdom ended in that year.
accepted.tq: Check the linked event, title and consequence as one chronological cluster.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions which geographical feature?
accepted.x: The Pithapuram inscription of Velanati Prithvishvara mentions Kolleru Lake.
accepted.tq: Match the inscription with its distinctive geographical reference.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: Who among the following was Ganapatideva's general in the coastal campaign that began in 1201?
accepted.x: Mutyalachaundaraya served as Ganapatideva's general and took Divi during the coastal campaign beginning in 1201.
accepted.tq: Apply the who-did-what trap to distinguish a general from allied nobles.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the political arrangements made by Ganapatideva after the coastal campaign?
o: He married the daughters of Prithviswara and appointed Akkana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Pinnachodi and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Mummadi Rajendra Chola and appointed Bayyana as Gajasahani.
He married the daughters of Manumasiddhi and appointed Tikkana as Gajasahani.
accepted.x: Ganapatideva married Pinnachodi's daughters Narama and Perama, and appointed their brother Jayapa as Gajasahani, the chief of the elephant forces.
accepted.tq: Test a multi-person relationship by separating family ties from political office.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: The title Gajasahani, conferred by Ganapatideva on Jayapa, denoted the chief of the:
accepted.x: Gajasahani referred to the chief of the elephant force.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar military offices by their functional meaning.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: In 1257, Ganapatideva allied with Akkana and Bayyana against the enemies of Manumasiddhi and killed:
accepted.x: Ganapatideva, along with Akkana and Bayyana, killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola in 1257, bringing the final end of the Velanati Chodas.
accepted.tq: Combine the year, alliance and defeated ruler rather than relying on the battle alone.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: Tikkana dedicated his Nirvachanottara Ramayana to:
accepted.x: Tikkana dedicated the Nirvachanottara Ramayana to Manumasiddhi.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work–patron relationship to avoid ruler-name substitution.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the consequence of the Battle of Muttukur?
o: Nellore fell to the Pandyas in 1263.
The Kakatiyas captured Divi from the Pandyas in 1263.
The Velanati kingdom was founded in 1263.
Ganapatideva was released from Yadava captivity in 1263.
accepted.x: The Pandyas defeated Ganapatideva in 1263, and Nellore fell to them after the Battle of Muttukur.
accepted.tq: Link the battle with its immediate territorial consequence.
accepted.sec: Ganapatideva - Nellore Chodas, Velanati Chodas, battles and defeats

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Prola I bore the title Arigajakesari. Vikrama Chakri belonged to Beta II, Vidyabhushana to Rudradeva, and Andhra Deshadhiswara to Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure title–ruler pair and eliminate swapped holders.
accepted.sec: Titles of Kakatiya rulers → ruler

accepted.s: The title ‘Samadhigata Panchamahashabda’ was held by:
accepted.x: Prola I bore the title Samadhigata Panchamahashabda, along with Arigajakesari.
accepted.tq: Test an exact royal title against nearby Kakatiya rulers.
accepted.sec: Titles of Kakatiya rulers → ruler

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Chola Chamuvardhi — Beta I
2. Vikrama Chakri — Beta II
3. Vinaya Vibhushanudu — Rudradeva
4. Andhra Deshadhiswara — Ganapatideva
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. These titles belonged respectively to Beta I, Beta II, Rudradeva and Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Verify each title–ruler pair before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Titles of Kakatiya rulers → ruler

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the title Kumara Rudradeva is correct?
o: It was the feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas.
It was held by Rudradeva during his accession.
It was the title of Ganapatideva after his victory over the Pandyas.
It was held by Prataparudra II at the time of his accession.
accepted.x: Kumara Rudradeva was the title borne by Prataparudra II at his accession.
accepted.tq: Separate a personal accession title from titles of earlier Kakatiya rulers.
accepted.sec: Titles of Kakatiya rulers → ruler

accepted.s: Mahamandaleswara, in the Kakatiya context, was primarily:
o: A feudatory title of the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas
A title given to generals of the Nellore Chodas
A title of the sovereign Kakatiya emperor only
A religious title of Jain teachers
accepted.x: Mahamandaleswara was a feudatory title used by the Samanta Kakatiyas under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a feudatory designation from a sovereign royal title.
accepted.sec: Titles of Kakatiya rulers → ruler

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the two principal views regarding the progenitor of the Kakatiyas?
o: Prola I of Hanamkonda and Beta I of Orugallu
Kakara Gundana of Magallu and Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram
Rudradeva of Anumakonda and Ganapatideva of Motupalli
Danarnava of Vengi and Durjaya of Pithapuram
accepted.x: The progenitor is identified in different traditions as Kakara Gundana of Magallu or Venna Bhupati of Bayyaram.
accepted.tq: Compare competing origin traditions without treating one disputed view as exclusive.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s:
Arrange the following phases of Kakatiya political history in chronological order:
A. Sovereign phase
B. Samanta phase
C. Kalyani Chalukya overlordship
D. Rashtrakuta overlordship
accepted.x: The Kakatiyas were first under the Rashtrakutas, then the Kalyani Chalukyas; the Samanta phase lasted from 956 to 1162, followed by the sovereign phase from 1163 to 1323.
accepted.tq: Fix the first overlord and then place the feudatory and sovereign phases.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: The Samanta and sovereign phases of Kakatiya history are conventionally dated respectively as:
accepted.x: The Samanta phase extended from 956 to 1162, while the sovereign phase extended from 1163 to 1323.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adjacent chronological ranges by their boundary years.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the principal overlordship of the early Kakatiyas?
o: Rashtrakutas followed by Eastern Chalukyas only
accepted.x: The early Kakatiyas were first feudatories of the Rashtrakutas and later of the Kalyani Chalukyas. The Eastern Chalukya association occurs in the context of the Magallu grant and may appear as an alternative in some questions.
accepted.tq: Separate the general sequence of overlordship from the issuer of the first inscription.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the early Kakatiyas:
1. They belonged to the Shudra social category.
2. Sanskrit was their official language.
3. Their early emblem under Rashtrakuta overlordship was Garuda.
4. The emblem changed to Varaha under the Kalyani Chalukyas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the Kakatiyas are described as Shudras, used Sanskrit officially, used Garuda during the Rashtrakuta phase and Varaha during the Kalyani Chalukya phase.
accepted.tq: Use the change in emblem to test the broader social and administrative description.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the religious development associated with the early Kakatiyas?
o: They were initially Shaivas and later became Jains.
They remained exclusively Buddhist throughout their history.
They were initially Vaishnavas and later became Buddhists.
They were initially Jains and later became Shaivas.
accepted.x: The early Kakatiyas were Jains and later adopted Shaivism. Their clan deity Kakatamma was identified with the Jain Kushmandini and was absorbed into Hinduism as Kakati Devi.
accepted.tq: Use the direction of religious change to reject reversed alternatives.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: ‘Kakati’ in the explanation of the Kakatiya clan deity is associated with which meaning?
accepted.x: Kakati means gourd. Kakatamma, or Kakati Devi, was associated with the Jain Kushmandini before being absorbed into Hindu tradition.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the exact etymological meaning from emblem and deity associations.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: The Bayyaram inscription traces the Kakatiya line to:
accepted.x: The Bayyaram inscription traces the Kakatiya lineage to Durjaya.
accepted.tq: Match the genealogy with the inscription that preserves it.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: The early territorial base of the Kakatiyas was known as:
accepted.x: The early Kakatiya base was Hanamkonda Vishaya, corresponding broadly to modern Karimnagar, Warangal and Khammam areas.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the early territorial base from later campaign regions.
accepted.sec: Origin debate - overlords, clan and caste, early religion

accepted.s: Which inscription is correctly matched with its issuer and historical significance?
o: Magallu grant — Eastern Chalukya Danarnava — first mention of the Kakatiya family
Bayyaram inscription — Rudradeva — protection to foreign traders
Motupalli inscription — Mailamba — best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Thousand Pillar inscription — Ganapatideva — first mention of Gundyana
accepted.x: The Magallu grant of Eastern Chalukya Danarnava, dated 956, contains the first mention of the Kakatiya family through Gundyana.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive first-mention fact and eliminate exchanged issuers.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: The Magallu grant, dated 956, was issued by:
accepted.x: The Magallu grant of 956 was issued by Eastern Chalukya Danarnava.
accepted.tq: Pair the date, issuer and first-mention inscription as a single unit.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Bayyaram tank inscription — 1219 — genealogy of the early Kakatiyas
Palampet inscription — 1213 — Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign
Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam — 1244 — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
accepted.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 concerns protection for foreign traders. Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya is associated with the Sanigaram inscription.
accepted.tq: Find the one exchanged fact in an inscription–date–content set.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by:
accepted.x: The Draksharamam inscription of 1158 was issued by Minister Inangala Brahma Reddi and records Rudradeva's accession.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an inscription issued by a minister from those issued by rulers.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Thousand Pillar inscription is correct?
1. It is also known as the Anumakonda inscription.
2. It is dated 1163.
3. It is associated with Rudradeva.
4. It records the declaration of independence.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The Anumakonda or Thousand Pillar inscription of 1163 is associated with Rudradeva and records Kakatiya independence.
accepted.tq: Combine alternative names, date, ruler and political significance before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: The Anumakonda inscription was found by J. S. Fleet and composed by:
accepted.x: J. S. Fleet discovered the Anumakonda inscription, and Achitendru composed it.
accepted.tq: Separate the discoverer from the composer of an inscription.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by:
accepted.x: The Bayyaram tank inscription of 1219 was issued by Mailamba, Ganapatideva's sister, and provides the best genealogy of the early Kakatiyas.
accepted.tq: Test kinship relations together with the inscription issuer.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: Which inscription is associated with Recherla Rudra and the Ramappa temple?
accepted.x: The Palampet inscription of 1213 is associated with Recherla Rudra and records the Ramappa temple during Ganapati's reign.
accepted.tq: Identify the monument inscription by pairing its place, date and patron.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam of 1244 primarily provided:
o: A record of the first mention of Gundyana
A genealogy of the Kakatiya family
A declaration of independence from the Chalukyas
accepted.x: The Motupalli Abhaya Sasanam issued by Ganapatideva in 1244 provided protection for foreign traders.
accepted.tq: Infer the purpose of a charter from its distinctive administrative provision.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. Sanigaram — Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya
2. Palampet — Ramappa temple
3. Dharmasagara — Jalakaranda
4. Pithapuram — Kolleru Lake
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct. These inscriptions respectively refer to Jain Juddha Mallajinalaya, the Ramappa temple, Jalakaranda and Kolleru Lake.
accepted.tq: Use distinctive cultural and geographical references to secure the inscription pairs.
accepted.sec: Inscriptions → ruler + first mention
